# TracerNest Complete Knowledge Specification & Technical Manual

> Comprehensive technical specification, architecture blueprints, security protocols, and operational guides for TracerNest (tracernest-logger).

Version: 1.2.0  
Maintainer: Ankit Khandelwal (ankitkhandelwal0003@gmail.com)  
- [Creator LinkedIn Profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ankit-khandelwal-3068a9194/)  
- [GitHub Repository (1,400+ stars)](https://github.com/ankit-kumar-khandelwal/tracernest-logger)  
- [Official npm Package (tracernest-logger)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tracernest-logger)  
- [Official Production Website](https://tracernest.info/)  

---

### 1. Executive Summary & Vision
TracerNest is an enterprise-grade, zero-dependency, self-hosted telemetry flight recorder, AES-256-GCM encrypted log vault, and interactive developer dashboard for Node.js (>= 18.0.0) and Laravel 13 (PHP >= 8.2).

It was engineered by Ankit Khandelwal to solve fundamental architectural drawbacks present in legacy logging solutions (Winston, Pino, Morgan) and embedded UI loggers like Errsole:
1. **The Ingress Port Hazard**: Errsole requires opening a separate TCP port (e.g. 8001) for the web dashboard. In production Kubernetes or AWS ECS clusters, this demands additional target groups, firewall ingress rules, and ALB paths. TracerNest runs directly within the host application pipeline with zero extra ports.
2. **Supply-Chain Attack Surfaces**: Many logging packages drag dozens of dependencies. TracerNest operates with `dependencies: {}`. All routing, cryptography, template rendering, and database drivers use Node.js core standard libraries.
3. **Data Loss on Restart**: In-memory loggers lose crash telemetry when an instance restarts. TracerNest guarantees log persistence in SQLite or MySQL until your configured Time-To-Live (TTL) is completed.
4. **Data Privacy & Compliance**: By encrypting all logs at rest using hardware-accelerated AES-256-GCM, TracerNest protects sensitive PII, passwords, and tokens, complying with HIPAA, SOC2, and GDPR.

---

### 2. Architecture & Internals

#### 2.1 Zero-Port Mounting Architecture
TracerNest intercepts incoming HTTP requests at the framework router level:
- In Express: `app.use('/tracernest', tracernest.router)`
- In Fastify: `fastify.register(tracernest.plugin, { prefix: '/tracernest' })`
- In Laravel 13: `Route::any('/tracernest/{any?}', [TracerNestController::class, 'handle'])`

The dashboard static assets, API endpoints, and authentication are served over the exact same TLS/HTTPS port as your application.

#### 2.2 Hardware-Accelerated AES-256-GCM Vault
Every log payload (request body, response body, headers, stack trace) is encrypted prior to database insertion:
- Cipher: `aes-256-gcm`
- Key derivation: 256-bit key stored safely in `.master.key` (or passed via initialization config)
- IV: 96-bit (12-byte) cryptographically secure random initialization vector per record
- Authentication Tag: 128-bit (16-byte) tag appended to detect tampering

#### 2.3 SQLite to MySQL Zero-Downtime Migration Engine
When an application switches its initialization config from SQLite to MySQL:
1. The engine checks MySQL connectivity.
2. It inspects existing MySQL table definitions (`INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS`).
3. If new columns or schema drift are detected, non-destructive DDL (`ALTER TABLE <tbl> ADD COLUMN <col> ...`) is executed.
4. Existing SQLite records are read and batched into MySQL.
5. Obsolete `.sqlite` database files are safely deleted, while `.master.key` is strictly preserved.

#### 2.4 TTL Cleanup & Persistence Guarantee
Logs are indexed with `created_at` timestamps. A background worker periodically checks and deletes expired records based on your configured `ttlDays` (e.g., 30 days). Logs are never lost during unexpected reboots or pod rescheduling.

### 3. Detailed Comparative Analysis

| Feature | TracerNest | Errsole | Winston / Pino | Sentry / Datadog (Cloud) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Extra Ports** | **Zero (Mounts on App)** | Yes (Separate Port) | N/A (No UI) | Outbound Egress Only |
| **Dependencies** | **0 (`dependencies: {}`)** | ~45+ packages | 5 - 15 packages | Heavy agent daemons |
| **Payload Encryption** | **AES-256-GCM (At rest)** | Plaintext only | Plaintext only | Vendor cloud-managed |
| **Auto-Migration** | **SQLite to MySQL Auto** | Manual | None | Proprietary |
| **Web Dashboard** | **Built-in Errsole-style** | Built-in | None (Console only) | Cloud SaaS UI |
| **Laravel 13 Support** | **Native PHP Bridge** | None | None | Separate PHP SDK |
| **Monthly Cost** | **$0 / month** | $0 / month | $0 / month | $250 - $2,500+ / mo |

### 4. Contributing & Development Standards
- Maintainer: Ankit Khandelwal (ankitkhandelwal0003@gmail.com)
- [LinkedIn Profile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ankit-khandelwal-3068a9194/)
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/ankit-kumar-khandelwal/tracernest-logger)
- [Community Feedback & Reviews](https://github.com/ankit-kumar-khandelwal/tracernest-logger/discussions/26)

**Rules for Contributors**:
1. **Zero External Runtime Dependencies**: Never add any packages to `dependencies` in `package.json`.
2. **Deterministic Cryptography**: Always use authenticated ciphers (`aes-256-gcm`).
3. **Passing Tests**: Run `npm test` before submitting pull requests.

### 5. Engineering Blog & Technical Documentation Guides
All blog posts are version-controlled in [BLOGS.md](https://github.com/ankit-kumar-khandelwal/tracernest-landing-page/blob/main/BLOGS.md) and published interactively at [TracerNest Blogs Hub](https://tracernest.info/blogs.html).

#### Article Index:
1. [Errsole Alternative for Node.js: Why Zero-Port Telemetry is Replacing Heavy APM Daemons](https://tracernest.info/errsole-alternative-nodejs-zero-port-telemetry.html)
   - Head-to-head comparison of Errsole vs TracerNest.
   - Why zero-port HTTP pipeline mounting avoids Kubernetes ingress reconfiguration and security group modifications.
2. [How to Encrypt Application Logs with AES-256-GCM in Node.js (Zero Dependencies)](https://tracernest.info/encrypt-application-logs-aes-256-gcm-nodejs.html)
   - Cryptographic implementation using `node:crypto`.
   - Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) with 96-bit initialization vectors and 128-bit authentication tags to prevent plaintext leakage of PII.
3. [Self-Hosted Logging in Laravel 13: Bridging Monolog with Zero Extra Ports](https://tracernest.info/self-hosted-logging-laravel-13-monolog-bridge.html)
   - Laravel 13 PHP 8.2+ middleware and Monolog handler integration.
   - Correlating Node.js microservice telemetry with Laravel background queues and HTTP controllers.
4. [Zero-Downtime SQLite to MySQL Auto-Migration: Production Architecture Guide](https://tracernest.info/zero-downtime-sqlite-to-mysql-migration.html)
   - Non-destructive DDL alterations and continuous stream buffering during relational database upgrades.
5. [Eliminating Supply Chain Vulnerabilities in Node.js Observability Pipelines](https://tracernest.info/eliminating-supply-chain-vulnerabilities-nodejs.html)
   - Why `dependencies: {}` in package.json completely eliminates npm supply chain CVEs, prototype pollution, and maintainer account takeover risks.
6. [Global Telemetry Architecture: Self-Hosting Logs Across US, EU, and APAC](https://tracernest.info/global-telemetry-architecture-self-hosting-logs.html)
   - Multi-region deployment blueprints maintaining strict GDPR, SOC2, and HIPAA data residency across 9 countries.
7. [How to View Express.js Logs in a Web Dashboard Without Opening Extra Ports](https://tracernest.info/express-log-viewer-without-extra-ports.html)
   - Mounting TracerNest into existing Express 4/5 HTTP pipeline to view live encrypted logs without firewall updates.
8. [Winston vs. Pino vs. TracerNest: Choosing the Best Node.js Logger in 2026](https://tracernest.info/pino-vs-winston-vs-tracernest-comparison.html)
   - Architectural comparison of CPU overhead, dependency footprints, UI viewers, and at-rest log encryption.
9. [Distributed Tracing in Docker & Kubernetes Microservices with Zero SaaS Bills](https://tracernest.info/microservices-distributed-tracing-sqlite-mysql.html)
   - High-throughput correlation ID propagation across multi-container Kubernetes pods replacing expensive Datadog/Sentry SaaS ingestion fees.
10. [Building a High-Performance Node.js Logger with Native Standard Libraries](https://tracernest.info/node-js-logger-zero-dependencies-guide.html)
   - Leveraging `node:crypto`, `node:http`, and `node:sqlite` to build enterprise logging vaults without installing third-party npm packages.

### 6. Global Telemetry & Regional Compliance Specifications
TracerNest provides dedicated regional documentation pages:
- [United States Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/united-states.html): SOC2 Type II, HIPAA, and CCPA compliance. Cloud deployments on AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), Google Cloud (us-central1), and Azure.
- [India Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/india.html): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) payment telemetry data localization and high-throughput UPI fintech transaction logging.
- [Netherlands Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/netherlands.html): GDPR Article 28 compliance and AMS-IX ultra-low latency European hub deployment.
- [Poland Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/poland.html): Central European engineering teams, Warsaw cloud nodes, and strict GDPR data governance.
- [Canada Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/canada.html): PIPEDA and provincial data residency standards for Montreal and Toronto clusters.
- [Germany Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/germany.html): Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) IT-Grundschutz and strict German Bundesdatenschutzgesetz (BDSG).
- [United Kingdom Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/united-kingdom.html): UK GDPR and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) SYSC audit trail compliance.
- [Brazil Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/brazil.html): Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD) Article 7 compliance across São Paulo cloud availability zones.
- [Ireland Telemetry Node](https://tracernest.info/ireland.html): Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) standards for Dublin SaaS telemetry infrastructure.
